subject: Re: Aria Solutions — publicity request tied to discount/concession
messages:
From: Jared Liu <jared@aria.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot pricing + case study / logo use

Hi Stephanie / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers and the routing options. We’re close to getting internal approval, but procurement is asking for a concession on list price for the 12-month pilot.

We would be willing to provide a formal case study and public logo placement (homepage partner section + one co-branded blog post) in exchange for a one-time concession on the pilot price. I attached a short brief on what Aria would include.

Can you confirm if Redwood would accept that trade (publicity + 2–3 quotes from our CPO) in return for a 30% discount on the pilot? If yes, we’ll pull together the marketing assets and timeline.

Attachment: aria_case_brief.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Jared
Jared Liu
Head of Procurement, Aria Solutions

Jared — thanks for the brief and the ask. Appreciate the clarity.

Quick answers:
- We’re open to a publicity-for-discount trade, but need clear guardrails (term length, approval rights, non-exclusivity).
- Any concession >20% requires executive deal-desk sign-off. I’m looping in Vivek (VP, Revenue) to approve the commercial tradeoff and final terms.

Proposed next steps (fast path):
1) Aria confirms the exact logo placements, quote text, and expected publish dates.
2) Redwood legal gets final review of the case study language and approvals process.
3) If Vivek signs off, we’ll update the pricing term sheet and SOW (no changes to data residency or SLAs).

For transparency, CC’ing Vivek now. Laura — can you and marketing prepare a draft one-page case acceptance checklist we can send to Jared?

Attachment: redwood_logo_guidelines.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot pricing + case study / logo use — exec approval request

Vivek / Laura — forwarding Aria’s ask and the brief. High level: Aria is asking for a 30% concession on the 12-month pilot in exchange for a co-branded case study, homepage logo placement, and 2–3 public quotes from their C-suite.

Why this matters: the deal is ~ $220k ARR if we convert after pilot. The pilot itself is a moderately sized purchase (~$36k list over 12 months). The 30% concession would materially reduce initial revenue and set a precedent for future pilots in this vertical.

Suggested guardrails for approval consideration:
- Limit publicity rights to 12 months from first publication (no perpetual rights).
- Redwood final approval on quotes and all creative assets prior to publish.
- No exclusivity clause; Aria cannot use competitive claims.
- Discount cap: if approved, recommend 25% max rather than 30%; require upfront signature on an amendment and a marketing schedule.
- If we agree to the logo placement + blog, require a joint press plan (date windows) and a short case acceptance form signed by both parties.

Attachments: price_term_sheet.xlsx (xlsx), aria_case_brief.pdf (pdf)

Can you advise: are you comfortable approving 25% with these guardrails? If yes, I’ll draft the amendment and marketing checklist and route for signatures (DocuSign).

— Stephanie
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 13:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot pricing + case study / logo use — exec approval request

Thanks for the context, Stephanie. I reviewed the numbers and the ask. I’m prepared to approve a concession tied to publicity with the following explicit constraints:

1) Discount approved: 25% off list for the 12-month pilot (not 30%).
2) Publicity scope: single case study + homepage logo tile + one co-authored blog post. No additional quotes or testimonial amplification without separate sign-off.
3) Term: public usage rights granted for 12 months from publication; rights revert to Redwood after that window. No perpetual rights.
4) Approval: Redwood must approve the final copy/visuals before publish. Legal to sign off on a short publicity addendum incorporated into the SOW.
5) Metrics: any customer-provided metrics cited in the case study must be corroborated by Aria and agreed in writing; if sensitive numbers are requested, we can require anonymization.

Please proceed as follows:
- Stephanie: draft a one-paragraph amendment that lists the concession, the publicity deliverables, and the 12-month window. Include legal and marketing contacts for approvals.
- Laura: prepare the marketing checklist and a short asset approval template.
- Stephanie: send the amendment via DocuSign and reference HubSpot deal ARIA-0142.

When the above are in place and Aria confirms assets/times, we can cut the discount and sign. This is a narrow, precedent-conscious approval — do not generalize.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Revenue | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com
